questions.prompt: Which of these run on the browser's single main thread?

options.text: JavaScript, style calculation, layout, paint, and event handling — all serialized

questions.explanation: The main thread serializes JS execution, style/layout/paint, and event handling, so a long task on it blocks rendering and input alike.

questions.prompt: What can a Web Worker NOT do?

options.text: Run JavaScript on a separate thread

questions.explanation: Workers run JS off the main thread and communicate via postMessage, but they cannot touch the DOM — DOM updates must happen back on the main thread.

questions.prompt: Reading a layout property (like offsetHeight) immediately after a style write forces the browser to do a synchronous ____ (recompute the layout).
questions.explanation: That pattern is forced synchronous layout (layout thrashing); doing it in a loop causes repeated reflows and turns a quick update into a long task.

questions.prompt: Match each tool to its best use.

pairs.right: Visual updates just before the next paint
Low-priority background work during idle time
Heavy, DOM-free computation off the main thread
Send data between the page and a worker

questions.explanation: rAF aligns with the frame, rIC uses idle time, a Web Worker offloads computation, and postMessage is how they communicate.

questions.prompt: Which techniques reduce pressure on the main thread? Select all that apply.

options.text: Break up long tasks and yield between chunks
Move heavy DOM-free computation to a Web Worker
Read and write layout properties interleaved in a loop

questions.explanation: Chunking, offloading to workers, and batching reads/writes all free the main thread. Interleaving reads and writes causes layout thrashing.

questions.prompt: Order the steps to fix a resize handler that thrashes layout.

items.text: Throttle so it runs at most once per frame

questions.explanation: Batch reads then writes to avoid forced reflows, align the update to the frame with rAF, and throttle so it runs at most once per frame.
